newsitem.title: USA: Pinellas Cty, Fla., approves sales tax extension.
newsitem.headline: Pinellas Cty, Fla., approves sales tax extension.

text.p: Voters in Florida's Pinellas County approved a 10-year extension of a one-cent sales tax for road, park and infrastructure projects, elections officials said Wednesday.

The "Penny for Pinellas" extension passed with 65 percent of the votes in Tuesday's election. It is expected to raise $1.4 billion over 10 years, with revenues divided among the county and its 24 municipalities.
The extension keeps the county's sales tax rate at seven percent. It would have dropped to six percent in 2000 if voters had rejected the extension.
Also Tuesday, voters in the City of St. Petersburg re-elected Mayor Dave Fischer to another four-year term. He garnered 53.5 percent of the vote, defeating retired Army general Bill Klein.
Fischer was first elected mayor in 1991, and was re-elected in 1993 when the city switched to four-year terms and adopted a strong-mayor form of government.
